papers.title: Long Shape Memory Alloy Tendon-based Soft Robotic Actuators and Implementation as a Soft Gripper
papers.robot_type: soft robotic actuators and soft gripper
actuation: Shape memory alloy (SMA) wire tendons (Flexinol LT, Dynalloy)
Joule heating / electric current actuation (0.95 A)
modeling_methods: Quasi-static beam bending equilibrium model equating SMA wire actuation stress with polymeric matrix bending resistance
Actuator center plane strain and SMA wire plane strain calculation using linear elastic cross-sectional beam properties (eccentricity, Young's modulus, cross-sectional area, and moment of inertia)
Geometric kinematic relation between matrix length, tendon length, actuator plane strain, and net SMA wire strain
Brinson one-dimensional thermoconstitutive model for SMA stress-strain-temperature behavior with cosine-based martensite fraction evolution during strain recovery
performance_metrics: Maximum bending angle (degrees)
Tip force as a function of bending angle (N)
Maximum gripper pulling force (N)
Sustained displacement under tensile load before grip failure (mm)
Maximum payload capacity / gripped object weight (g and kg)
Actuation response time to reach full deformation (s)
Cyclic durability (number of cycles without degradation of maximum bending angle)

evidence_claims.title: Long Shape Memory Alloy Tendon-based Soft Robotic Actuators and Implementation as a Soft Gripper
evidence_claims.claim: Decoupling the length of the polymeric matrix from the SMA wire by using free-sliding tendons through silicone tubes enables large increases in bending angle (up to 400 degrees) and tip force (up to 0.89 N).

evidence_claims.title: Long Shape Memory Alloy Tendon-based Soft Robotic Actuators and Implementation as a Soft Gripper
evidence_claims.claim: A quasi-static mechanical model coupling beam strain mechanics with Brinson's 1D SMA constitutive model accurately predicts bending angle as a function of tendon length up to physical contact limits.

evidence_claims.title: Long Shape Memory Alloy Tendon-based Soft Robotic Actuators and Implementation as a Soft Gripper
evidence_claims.claim: Uneven tendon lengths on either side of the U-shaped routing produce pure planar bending without torsion due to tension distribution through free sliding in the silicone sleeve.

evidence_claims.title: Long Shape Memory Alloy Tendon-based Soft Robotic Actuators and Implementation as a Soft Gripper
evidence_claims.claim: Modular finger packaging with V-shaped bearings routes 300 mm tendons compactly and withstands 100 continuous thermal cycles without degradation of maximum bending angle.

evidence_claims.title: Long Shape Memory Alloy Tendon-based Soft Robotic Actuators and Implementation as a Soft Gripper
evidence_claims.claim: Three-fingered antagonistic and triangular soft grippers adaptively grasp diverse objects weighing from 5 g up to 1.5 kg (and withstand a 2 kg test weight).

evidence_claims.title: Long Shape Memory Alloy Tendon-based Soft Robotic Actuators and Implementation as a Soft Gripper
evidence_claims.claim: The soft gripper achieves maximum pulling forces of 25 N in point contact and 30 N in power grasp using 0.305 mm SMA wires, maintaining high force over 40 mm displacement.

evidence_claims.title: Long Shape Memory Alloy Tendon-based Soft Robotic Actuators and Implementation as a Soft Gripper
evidence_claims.claim: Wrapping actuator fingers in a low-friction TPU-coated sleeve drops maximum pulling force from 25-30 N to 7-13 N, demonstrating the critical role of interfacial friction in load capacity.

evidence_claims.title: Long Shape Memory Alloy Tendon-based Soft Robotic Actuators and Implementation as a Soft Gripper
evidence_claims.claim: The modular soft gripper can be integrated as an end-effector on a commercial 6-DOF industrial robot arm (UR10) to execute pick-and-place tasks on real-world objects.

limitations.text: Actuator bending deformation can be physically limited by the actuator contacting its own driving tendons, the mounting jig, or folding onto itself
Tip force measurement was restricted to a maximum angle of 120° due to physical space limitations for positioning the load cell
Heat accumulation inside the matrix during repeated cycling causes an increase in the minimum unactuated bending angle during cooling
Thinner actuators exhibit poorer tip force transmission compared to thicker actuators due to intermediate compliance between base and tip
High pulling forces rely heavily on friction; reducing surface friction drastically reduces pulling capacity
Increasing wire diameter, wire count, or tendon length escalates electrical power demands and increases risk of heat accumulation
Standard Joule heating may become speed- and efficiency-limited when scaling to extremely long SMA wire lengths
Actuation speed remains slower than pneumatic actuators, requiring further design refinements before competing in high-speed industrial environments

The quasi-static mechanical model ignores dynamic inertial forces, rate-dependent viscoelastic effects of PDMS, frictional dissipation between sliding wire and silicone tube, and 3D contact mechanics during grasping
Actuation is entirely open-loop (constant current and duration), lacking closed-loop force, position, or temperature feedback control
Passive cooling (9 s cooling required for 1 s heating) severely limits actuation frequency to approximately 0.1 Hz
Routing long wires over mechanical V-shaped bearings introduces mechanical complexity, potential friction losses, and mechanical wear not present in monolithic soft actuators

future_work.text: Improving the gripper to produce faster actuation and stronger grasping forces for industrial applications
Investigating active cooling mechanisms for the tendons to prevent excessive heat accumulation in the matrix and module housing
Exploring alternative heating methods beyond Joule heating to enhance heating speed and energy efficiency for extremely long SMA wires
Optimizing polymeric matrix geometry and cross-sectional profile in tandem with long SMA tendons to further enhance performance
Redesigning the module to be more compact using stiffer materials, smaller bearings, and optimized tendon arrangements
Adapting the long-tendon architecture to other robotic devices, mechanisms, and medical tools

gap_implications.text: Decoupling smart-material stroke from structural body length via low-friction sliding channels provides a generalizable design paradigm for overcoming intrinsic strain limits in 1D smart materials without sacrificing cross-sectional stiffness

However, scaling tendon length increases thermal mass and cooling latency under Joule heating, highlighting an unresolved trade-off between stroke magnification and cycle bandwidth in thermally driven soft robotics
The reliance on high interfacial friction for payload retention underscores the need for integrating active variable-friction surfaces or mechanical interlocks in tendon-driven soft grippers

papers.title: Soft Robotic Grippers Based on Particle Transmission
actuation: piston actuation driven by an electric motor
modeling_methods: Kinematic volume-expansion modeling linking injected volume ratio to torus-segment bending angle under constant perimeter constraints
Constitutive stress modeling of the silicone unit cell using incompressible Neo-Hookean hyperelastic strain energy and the Young-Laplace equation
Inter-particle contact mechanics modeling normal forces, sliding friction, and resultant resistive friction moments summed across particle layers to determine rotational stiffness
performance_metrics: Bending range of motion / angle α (degrees)
Rotational stiffness SR (FlF / β in N·m/rad or equivalent)
Fold change in rotational stiffness (ratio relative to initial state or fluid baselines)
Input piston force vs. output actuation force (N)
Motion repeatability / standard deviation of bending angle (degrees)
Restoration / retract angle (degrees) with and without vibration

evidence_claims.title: Soft Robotic Grippers Based on Particle Transmission
evidence_claims.claim: Using particle transmission driven by a motor-actuated piston circumvents fluid-sealing challenges while enabling combined actuation and variable stiffness without bulky pumps or valve manifolds.

evidence_claims.title: Soft Robotic Grippers Based on Particle Transmission
evidence_claims.claim: Injecting solid particles up to 1.8 times the initial volume produces bending up to 60 degrees and increases rotational stiffness by nearly seven-fold from the unactuated state.

evidence_claims.title: Soft Robotic Grippers Based on Particle Transmission
evidence_claims.claim: Kinematic bending range and rotational stiffness can be modeled analytically by assuming torus segment expansion and calculating inter-particle contact forces and friction moments from Neo-Hookean membrane tension.

evidence_claims.title: Soft Robotic Grippers Based on Particle Transmission
evidence_claims.claim: Solid glassy glass balls demonstrated superior performance over stainless steel balls, plastic balls, and beans owing to high hardness, low thermal conductivity, and small friction coefficient.

evidence_claims.title: Soft Robotic Grippers Based on Particle Transmission
evidence_claims.claim: Smaller particle diameters (2 mm vs. 3 mm and 4 mm) generate a more linear bending response, larger angular deflection, and higher rotational stiffness.

evidence_claims.title: Soft Robotic Grippers Based on Particle Transmission
evidence_claims.claim: At an injected volume ratio of 1.8, particle transmission generates nearly six-fold greater stiffness and over five-fold greater bending deflection than compressed air, and roughly three-fold higher stiffness than water.

evidence_claims.title: Soft Robotic Grippers Based on Particle Transmission
evidence_claims.claim: Incomplete elastic restoration occurs after piston retraction due to inter-particle jamming, but embedding miniature vibrators into the strain-limiting layer enables complete recovery to the initial position.

limitations.text: Actuator range of motion reaches an upper limit around a volume ratio of 1.8 where force chains cause particles to behave as a rigid solid, resisting further bending and risking membrane rupture near the inlet
Bending angle of the prototype actuator is relatively small (around 90°), requiring an additional mechanism to grasp large objects
The actuator cannot fully restore to its unactuated baseline without active external vibration due to particle jamming and limited silicone restoring force
Introduced vibration may be undesirable in certain operating environments
Optimal power and frequency for the embedded vibrators were not determined
High stiffness increase may be unsuitable for delicate objects requiring gentle contact, such as eggs
Actuation output force is significantly lower than input piston force because much of the input work is redirected into particle jamming
Motion accuracy and repeatability degrade as injected volume increases (standard deviation increases up to 3° at V = 1.8)
Analytical model treats deformation as an idealized uniform torus and ignores localized bulging, cylinder wall friction, and dynamic granular packing effects
Integrating rigid electric drive cylinders and vibration motors introduces rigid elements, mass, and wiring that compromise the total compliance and compactness of the soft robotic system
Long-term durability, cyclic fatigue of the silicone membrane, particle wear, and actuation speed/bandwidth were not evaluated

future_work.text: Investigating the optimum operating power and vibration frequency of the embedded vibrators for actuator restoration
Further exploring the mechanics of particle chain formation and destruction under granular mechanics principles

gap_implications.text: Demonstrates that dry granular materials can act simultaneously as an actuation transmission medium and a variable stiffness mechanism, bypassing the need for fluid seals and pneumatic pumps; however, this single study does not prove general suitability across all soft robotics due to motion range saturation and the necessity of auxiliary vibrators for restoration.

papers.title: A Dexterous Soft Robotic Hand for Delicate In-Hand Manipulation
stiffness_mechanism: structural compliance from bellows geometry and silicone elastomer
actuation: pneumatic actuation (positive pressure and vacuum) using two side-by-side air chambers per finger
modeling_methods: Least-squares circular fitting applied to three tracked marker coordinates along the finger to measure curvature under varying actuation pressure
Quasi-static kinematic assumption for slow commanded finger motion profiles
Kinematic contact assumption of rolling without slip at the fingertip interface
No analytical or numerical constitutive mechanics models (e.g., beam theory, hyperelastic strain-energy functions, or finite element models) were formulated
performance_metrics: Maximum blocked output force: 2.3 N (grasping axis, dual-chamber actuation), 0.8 N (grasping axis, single-chamber), 1.2 N (lateral axis, single-chamber)
Unactuated finger stiffness: 44.5 ± 3.7 N/m (grasping axis), 209.6 ± 13.9 N/m (side-to-side lateral axis)
Burst pressure: 310 kPa (maximum operating pressure 240 kPa; nominal grasping pressure 138 kPa)
Maximum grip strength: 4.7 N with 4 fingers and soft pads at 173 kPa (holding objects up to 0.47 kg); 0.21 N without soft pads
Off-axis grasp stiffness: 30–35 N/m at 90-degree perpendicular orientation
Planar translation workspace: ~50 mm diameter circular region across test objects
Extraneous lateral drift during rotation: within 12 mm across all objects
Continuous rotation gait displacement: average angular displacement per cycle across 20 cycles per object (ranging from ~10 to 45 deg/cycle depending on diameter)

evidence_claims.title: A Dexterous Soft Robotic Hand for Delicate In-Hand Manipulation
evidence_claims.claim: Dual-chamber pneumatic bellows fingers provide two degrees of freedom per finger, achieving an 80 mm range in the primary grasping axis and ±30 mm of lateral range with roughly linear grasping curvature between 0 and 138 kPa.

evidence_claims.title: A Dexterous Soft Robotic Hand for Delicate In-Hand Manipulation
evidence_claims.claim: The soft finger design exhibits directional stiffness anisotropy, being roughly 4.7 times stiffer in the lateral axis (209.6 ± 13.9 N/m) than in the grasping axis (44.5 ± 3.7 N/m) in an unactuated state.

evidence_claims.title: A Dexterous Soft Robotic Hand for Delicate In-Hand Manipulation
evidence_claims.claim: Adding soft silicone fingertip pads (Eco-flex 00-30, Shore 00-30) increases hand grip strength by more than twentyfold (from 0.21 N to 4.7 N at 173 kPa for a four-finger grasp on a 76.2 mm cylinder) compared to bare/harder fingertips.

evidence_claims.title: A Dexterous Soft Robotic Hand for Delicate In-Hand Manipulation
evidence_claims.claim: A four-finger cross hand configuration executes planar translation across diverse object geometries within a similar circular workspace (~50 mm diameter), whereas rotational range scales inversely with object diameter.

evidence_claims.title: A Dexterous Soft Robotic Hand for Delicate In-Hand Manipulation
evidence_claims.claim: An open-loop heuristic finger gait parameterized solely by nominal pressure (pg) and differential pressure deviation (δ) achieves continuous 360-degree rotation across varied object shapes and sizes over 20 cycles without tactile feedback or trajectory re-planning.

evidence_claims.title: A Dexterous Soft Robotic Hand for Delicate In-Hand Manipulation
evidence_claims.claim: Finger droop caused by object mass under gravity can cause objects to be dropped during reorientation, but can be compensated by superimposing vertical translation pressure offsets onto the rotation gait.

limitations.text: Compliance causes significant finger droop under gravitational forces from object weight, which leads to dropped objects during rotation if not compensated
Passive compliance and open-loop control can fail without on-board sensing when loading conditions become unfavorable
System lacks on-board sensors for measuring finger shape or contact forces
No visual perception was integrated into the closed-loop system; object placement and arm poses were predefined
No mathematical models of finger motion were utilized for motion planning
The current palm is rigid rather than soft, which may limit manipulation performance
Smaller objects experience higher undesired angular deflection during translation due to rotational instabilities on high-curvature surfaces
There is an inherent trade-off between grasping force and lateral range of motion when chambers are actuated differentially
The quasi-static operation regime and slow pressure trajectories mean high-speed dynamic in-hand manipulation remains unverified
Maximum payload is restricted to under 0.5 kg (maximum grip strength ~4.7 N), limiting application to lightweight objects
The open-loop finger gait relies on rolling contact without slip; objects with low or uneven friction could experience unmodeled slip or loss of grasp stability
Long-term cyclic fatigue and durability of elastomer chambers, adhesive joints, and thread bindings under repetitive pressure/vacuum cycling were not characterized
Gravity compensation requires prior estimation or knowledge of object mass and hand orientation, lacking autonomous load sensing

future_work.text: Incorporating a soft palm constructed from compliant components to improve in-hand manipulation performance
Developing mathematical models of soft finger motion to enhance manipulation planning and execution
Integrating on-board sensing for finger shape and contact forces
Implementing closed-loop control of contact forces for scenarios where passive compliance alone fails
Applying dexterous soft robotic hands to assistive domestic tasks and bimanual manipulation platforms

gap_implications.text: While passive compliance and open-loop pressure control eliminate sensor complexity for basic manipulation primitives, the absence of closed-loop contact and shape sensing prevents autonomous slip detection and error recovery in unstructured settings.

Relying on hand-tuned heuristic pressure waypoints without predictive continuum or contact mechanics models restricts generalization to arbitrary three-dimensional manipulation trajectories or unknown object dynamics.
The necessity of manual gravity compensation using prior mass knowledge highlights an open gap in autonomous in-hand payload identification and real-time adaptive compliance control.

papers.title: A novel design of shape-memory alloy-based soft robotic gripper with variable stiffness
stiffness_mechanism: resistance wire (Ni-Cr) Joule heating and natural cooling
modeling_methods: Thermal heat transfer model of SMA wire considering Joule heating and convective cooling to ambient air
SMA hysteresis thermal phase transformation model (martensite-to-austenite and austenite-to-martensite kinetics)
SMA one-dimensional constitutive stress-strain formulation
Cantilever beam deflection model for the flexible joint under bending moment generated by SMA wire force
Ni-Cr wire electrical Joule heating and paraffin thermal absorption energy balance model
Kinematic model relating SMA wire shrinkage, joint deflection, and circular arc bending angle
Geometric gripping volume model determining minimum and maximum graspable object radii from base angle and finger dimensions
performance_metrics: Finger stiffness at high stiffness (K1 = 0.2431 N/mm) and low stiffness (K2 = 0.0136 N/mm), representing an 18-fold enhancement
Heating time to reach paraffin melting point (70 s) and cooling time to return to solid state (380 s)
Maximum reaction force at 10 mm displacement (2.21 N at high stiffness vs. 0.14 N at low stiffness)
Maximum vertical pulling force (8.73 N at high stiffness vs. 3.28 N at low stiffness)
Maximum grasping force (5.66 N at high stiffness vs. 0.57 N at low stiffness, ~10-fold ratio)
Theoretical object grasping diameter range (21 mm to 90 mm)
Maximum payload demonstrated without continuous SMA power (500 g water bottle)

evidence_claims.title: A novel design of shape-memory alloy-based soft robotic gripper with variable stiffness
evidence_claims.claim: A single robotic finger achieves an approximate 18-fold stiffness variation between the liquid state (0.0136 N/mm) and solid state (0.2431 N/mm) of paraffin.

evidence_claims.title: A novel design of shape-memory alloy-based soft robotic gripper with variable stiffness
evidence_claims.claim: Variable stiffness joints enhance the gripper's maximum grasping force by approximately 10-fold, increasing from 0.57 N at low stiffness to 5.66 N at high stiffness.

evidence_claims.title: A novel design of shape-memory alloy-based soft robotic gripper with variable stiffness
evidence_claims.claim: Paraffin heating to its melting point of 58 °C with an embedded Ni-Cr wire takes about 70 s at 10 V, while natural cooling to the solid state takes about 380 s.

evidence_claims.title: A novel design of shape-memory alloy-based soft robotic gripper with variable stiffness
evidence_claims.claim: Independently modulating the stiffness of two embedded joints per finger combined with SMA wire actuation enables four distinct configurations: straight, joint-1 bending, joint-2 bending, and simultaneous bending.

evidence_claims.title: A novel design of shape-memory alloy-based soft robotic gripper with variable stiffness
evidence_claims.claim: At high stiffness, the soft gripper can stably hold a 500 g water bottle even after turning off power to the SMA actuator wire.

evidence_claims.title: A novel design of shape-memory alloy-based soft robotic gripper with variable stiffness
evidence_claims.claim: An analytical framework couples SMA Joule heating, empirical phase transformation kinetics, constitutive stress-strain relationships, and cantilever beam mechanics to relate heating time to joint bending angle.

limitations.text: A long time is required for changing the joint from low stiffness to high stiffness (380 s cooling time), which increases the overall time needed to grasp objects.
Reliance on passive natural cooling results in a slow cycle time (380 s to stiffen), which severely restricts operating speed and dynamic grasping tasks.
Continuous electrical power is required to hold the deformed configuration during the multi-minute cooling phase before the paraffin solidifies.
Heat dissipation through the silicone encapsulation over repeated thermal cycles may affect surrounding structures and repeatable phase transformation temperatures.
The payload capacity (500 g) and maximum grasping force (5.66 N) remain relatively low for heavier robotic manipulation tasks.
Cantilever beam and circular arc assumptions do not capture 3D multi-axial deformations, contact compliance, or viscoelastic effects in the silicone casing.

future_work.text: Optimization and experiments to shorten the transition time required to change stiffness from low stiffness to high stiffness.

gap_implications.text: The long thermal relaxation time (~380 s) indicates that practical implementation of phase-change materials in soft robotics requires active cooling methods or hybrid mechanisms.

Simplifying assumptions in the joint model (ignoring heat dissipation through the elastomer and viscoelastic mechanics) suggest a need for comprehensive multi-physics thermo-mechanical models for encapsulated phase-change soft actuators.

The trade-off between compliance at low stiffness and modest maximum grasping force (5.66 N) highlights the potential for investigating hybrid rigid-soft reinforcement structures to achieve higher payloads.

papers.title: Design and Automatic Fabrication of Novel Bio-Inspired Soft Smart Robotic Hands
modeling_methods: Analytical rotational stiffness modeling combining moment equilibrium, geometrical kinematic relations of segmented arc bending, internal pneumatic pressure torque, and Coulomb friction work among jammed spherical particles.
Kinematic forward modeling of the three-joint finger based on rigid-link geometric transformations to estimate fingertip coordinates from individual joint angles.
Empirical polynomial regression (quadratic curve fitting) relating conductive TPU electrical resistance variations to joint bending rotation angles.
performance_metrics: Rotational stiffness (N*mm/rad)
Maximum holding weight / load capacity (kg)
Radius of curvature (mm)
Joint rotation angle (radians / degrees)
Sensor electrical resistance change (Delta R, ohms)
Fingertip tracking position coordinates (x, y, mm)

evidence_claims.title: Design and Automatic Fabrication of Novel Bio-Inspired Soft Smart Robotic Hands
evidence_claims.claim: Passive granular jamming induced by pressurized pneumatic actuation increases the rotational stiffness of the soft finger by 2.14 times (from 1223 N*mm/rad to 2621 N*mm/rad) at 450 kPa without requiring a dedicated vacuum source.

evidence_claims.title: Design and Automatic Fabrication of Novel Bio-Inspired Soft Smart Robotic Hands
evidence_claims.claim: Enclosing loose granular particles in the passive chamber increases the bending radius of curvature at lower pressures, but this discrepancy diminishes and becomes practically negligible at operating pressures around 400 to 450 kPa.

evidence_claims.title: Design and Automatic Fabrication of Novel Bio-Inspired Soft Smart Robotic Hands
evidence_claims.claim: A five-fingered soft robotic hand with particle-filled passive chambers achieved a maximum holding capacity of 1.452 kg compared to 0.8425 kg without particles at an actuation pressure of 450 kPa.

evidence_claims.title: Design and Automatic Fabrication of Novel Bio-Inspired Soft Smart Robotic Hands
evidence_claims.claim: An analytical rotational stiffness model combining air pressure torque and particle friction work accurately captures the experimental stiffness progression across increasing actuation pressures.

evidence_claims.title: Design and Automatic Fabrication of Novel Bio-Inspired Soft Smart Robotic Hands
evidence_claims.claim: Multi-material fused deposition modeling (FDM) enables single-process automatic additive fabrication of soft pneumatic elastomeric chambers and integrated conductive TPU piezoresistive position feedback sensors.

evidence_claims.title: Design and Automatic Fabrication of Novel Bio-Inspired Soft Smart Robotic Hands
evidence_claims.claim: Piezoresistive conductive TPU sensors embedded at finger joints demonstrate quadratic calibration relationships between resistance change and joint bending angles, allowing reconstruction of fingertip positions.

evidence_claims.title: Design and Automatic Fabrication of Novel Bio-Inspired Soft Smart Robotic Hands
evidence_claims.claim: Integrating an independently actuated soft palm capable of metacarpal bending and secondary bending facilitates effective grasping of geometrically diverse everyday objects.

limitations.text: Position feedback modules were only fabricated and evaluated on the index finger rather than all five fingers and palm.
Discrepancies between analytical stiffness predictions and experimental measurements arose from test errors and simplified modeling assumptions.
Deviations between visual ground truth and sensor-derived fingertip position tracking were caused by environmental disturbances and calibration inaccuracies.
Carbon black particles in the conductive TPU filament tend to clog FDM printer nozzles over extended printing periods, requiring nozzle cleaning with PLA.
Particles must be loaded manually into the passive chamber post-printing through a slot and sealed with hot melt adhesive.
Holding tests could not be performed below 325 kPa finger pressure because the finger bending curvature was insufficient to secure the grasped test object.
Stiffness variation is strictly coupled to the pneumatic actuation pressure, preventing independent control of joint stiffness and bending deflection.
Long-term electrical hysteresis, drift, and cyclic degradation of the 3D-printed conductive TPU piezoresistive sensors were not characterized.
Mechanical fatigue, wear, and airtightness durability of the FDM-printed NinjaFlex chambers subjected to repeated pressurization and particle contact friction were not evaluated.

Holding performance verification relied on an object specifically designed with raised surface features to enhance interlocking, which may not reflect grasping performance on smooth or low-friction surfaces.

future_work.text: Integrating position feedback sensing modules into all five fingers and the palm.
Implementing closed-loop position and trajectory control and developing sophisticated grasping strategies based on sensor feedback.
Integrating tactile sensors into the hand to provide more accurate touch and contact feedback.
Further investigating theoretical models of the passive jamming phenomenon to optimize structural hand performance.

gap_implications.text: Developing mechanisms that decouple variable stiffness from bending actuation to allow stiffness modulation at arbitrary finger postures.
Investigating fully automated manufacturing workflows capable of directly incorporating granular jamming media without manual filling and adhesive sealing steps.
Developing dynamic compensation and filtering algorithms to address piezoresistive sensor drift and hysteresis in additive soft robotics.

papers.title: Smart Soft Actuators and Grippers Enabled by Self-Powered Tribo-Skins
modeling_methods: Finite element method (FEM) using ABAQUS 6.14
Four-node tetrahedral element discretization for the soft actuator elastomer body
Hyperelastic constitutive modeling using the Ogden model
performance_metrics: Peak open-circuit voltage: up to 8 V for inner TENG; 4.8 V to 41 V for tribo-skin under 2–10 N force
Current output: 50–60 nA for tribo-skin at 8 N (1 Hz)
Transferred charge: ~7.5 nC for tribo-skin at 8 N (1 Hz)
Force sensing range: 2 N to 10 N (saturates above 10 N)
Endurance: stable voltage output over 1000 contact cycles at 1 Hz (~16.6 min)
Energy harvesting rate: 1.6 V stored on a 0.1 µF capacitor in 30 s
Grasp diameter range: 32 mm to 82 mm
Maximum grasping weight: ~500 g (with Dragon Skin 10)

evidence_claims.title: Smart Soft Actuators and Grippers Enabled by Self-Powered Tribo-Skins
evidence_claims.claim: Integration of cable-driven actuation with embedded contact–separation TENG strips and single-electrode tribo-skins enables concurrent actuation, self-powered bending sensing, and contact pressure sensing.

evidence_claims.title: Smart Soft Actuators and Grippers Enabled by Self-Powered Tribo-Skins
evidence_claims.claim: Finite element modeling with ABAQUS using four-node tetrahedral elements and a 3-term Ogden model accurately captures the nonlinear bending deformation and strain distribution of the notched silicone actuator under cable tension.

evidence_claims.title: Smart Soft Actuators and Grippers Enabled by Self-Powered Tribo-Skins
evidence_claims.claim: The inner TENG generates open-circuit voltage pulses whose peak amplitude scales with the bending angle α, reaching 8 V at 600° motor rotation.

evidence_claims.title: Smart Soft Actuators and Grippers Enabled by Self-Powered Tribo-Skins
evidence_claims.claim: Micropyramid-structured tribo-skin patches exhibit pressure-dependent electrical outputs from 4.8 V to 41 V as applied force increases from 2 N to 10 N at 1 Hz, with saturation occurring beyond 10 N.

evidence_claims.title: Smart Soft Actuators and Grippers Enabled by Self-Powered Tribo-Skins
evidence_claims.claim: Tribo-skin voltage output depends on contact frequency (increasing from 18.7 V to 23.6 V between 0.3 Hz and 2.2 Hz at 7 N) and contacting material composition, while demonstrating durability over 1000 cycles at 1 Hz.

evidence_claims.title: Smart Soft Actuators and Grippers Enabled by Self-Powered Tribo-Skins
evidence_claims.claim: A modular three-fingered soft gripper discriminates geometric contact sequences, detects object release and secondary impacts, and differentiates object mass based on voltage signal amplitudes.

evidence_claims.title: Smart Soft Actuators and Grippers Enabled by Self-Powered Tribo-Skins
evidence_claims.claim: Mechanical energy harvested during cyclic grasping charges a 0.1 µF capacitor through a rectifier bridge to 1.6 V in 30 s.

limitations.text: The electrical output of the inner TENG is not very competitive for energy harvesting due to relatively low grasping frequencies in practical applications
The sensing output of the single-electrode tribo-skin is strongly affected by external factors, including contacting object material, ambient humidity, and temperature
The contact area of the tribo-skin varies between partial and full surface depending on object geometry, presenting calibration challenges
The tribo-skin exhibits a sensing saturation limit for forces exceeding 10 N
Actuator extension relies passively on material elasticity, meaning return dynamics and straight-state recovery are slow and unactuated compared to cable-pulled flexion
Triboelectric voltage signals are fundamentally rate-dependent and transient, complicating sustained static force sensing during stationary holding without dynamic motion

Cross-sensitivity between contact material dielectric properties, contact surface area, and applied force makes isolated, deterministic force calibration difficult without prior knowledge of the target object
Maximum lifting capacity is restricted (approx. 500 g even when fabricated with stiffer Dragon Skin 10), limiting utility to lightweight handling

future_work.text: Developing the skin TENG using contact–separation mode rather than single-electrode mode to eliminate sensitivity to contact materials and ambient environmental factors like humidity
Integrating machine learning methods with sensory feedback to identify object features such as shape and hardness

gap_implications.text: Single-electrode triboelectric skins require decoupling strategies (such as enclosed contact-separation architectures or multi-modal tactile sensing) to prevent environmental humidity and target material composition from confounding force measurements
Dynamic triboelectric sensing mechanisms leave an open need for hybridizing with piezoresistive or capacitive modes to enable drift-free, long-duration static force feedback in soft end effectors
